title: Current faster than the boat?
hook: The river runs faster than your boat can go. Will you ever reach the other side?

knows: rivers flow and boats move through the water
doesNotKnow: relative velocity: the boat's velocity over the ground is its velocity in the water plus the current's
that motion across the river and along it are independent

misconception: A current faster than the boat stops it crossing, or at least makes the crossing take longer.
objective: The learner can explain that a boat pointed straight across crosses at its own speed whatever the current, so a 90 m river at 3 m/s takes 30 s; the current only sets how far downstream it lands.

claims.text: A boat pointed straight across a 90 m river at 3 m/s relative to the water reaches the far bank in 30 s, whatever the speed of the current.
claims.source: Ground velocity = boat velocity in the water + current velocity (Galilean addition). The current is along the river, so the across component stays 3 m/s: 90 / 3 = 30 s. Re-integrated in artifacts/scratch/w4phys/check.mjs (dt = 1e-4 s) for currents 0-6 m/s: 30.000 s each.

claims.text: In those 30 s a current of u m/s carries the boat 30 u metres downstream: 60 m at 2 m/s, 120 m at 4 m/s, 180 m at 6 m/s.
claims.source: x = u t at t = 30 s; same integration gives 0, 30, 60, 90, 120, 150, 180 m for u = 0..6 m/s.

claims.text: Every 10 s the boat is another 30 m across, at the same across-distance as a boat in still water.
claims.source: y = 3 t, independent of u: 30, 60, 90 m at 10, 20, 30 s. The stage draws these as dots on shared across-lines.

claims.text: The current pushes along the river, never across it, so it decides where the boat lands, not when.
claims.source: Independence of perpendicular velocity components (any introductory mechanics text, e.g. OpenStax University Physics Vol. 1, section 4.5 Relative Motion in One and Two Dimensions).

claims.text: Model: the current is the same everywhere and the boat always points straight across at 3 m/s; real rivers run slower near the banks.
claims.source: Stated on stage ('Uniform current') and in the reveal. Velocity in a real channel falls towards the banks and bed because of friction (no-slip boundary); with a non-uniform current the crossing time is still 90 / 3 s if the boat keeps pointing straight across, but the landing point changes.

recall.question: A swimmer swims straight across a 40 m river at 1 m/s through the water. The current is 2 m/s. How long does the crossing take?
recall.why: The current only carries the swimmer downstream; across the river they still move at 1 m/s, so 40 m takes 40 s.
